title: Is being thrifty a virtue?
reason: 上一课聚焦工作压力与恢复，今天轮换到金融、消费和资源取舍。本集梳理 thrift 从生活得好、节制消费到现代消费主义语境中的含义变化，适合联系个人储蓄、项目预算和平台资源规划。练习反复调用限制支出、为目标储蓄、满足基本需求和权衡边界等高频表达，帮助学习者把理解转化为简洁、可迁移的主动表达。

targetExpressions.meaning: reduce the amount of money I spend
targetExpressions.usage: Change the possessive for the speaker: We need to limit our spending this quarter.

targetExpressions.meaning: gradually collect enough money for an initial payment
targetExpressions.usage: Use save up for before a goal: She is saving up for a deposit on a flat.

targetExpressions.meaning: not required or pressured to do something
targetExpressions.usage: Follow it with a verb: A clear plan leaves the team free from the need to guess.

targetExpressions.expression: save up for a rainy day
targetExpressions.meaning: keep money for an unexpected future problem
targetExpressions.usage: Use it when discussing emergency savings: I save a little each month for a rainy day.

targetExpressions.meaning: provide the essential things needed to live
targetExpressions.usage: Use meet with needs or requirements: The budget must first meet basic needs.

targetExpressions.expression: a very fine line to tread
targetExpressions.meaning: a difficult balance between two close or competing positions
targetExpressions.usage: Use it when both extremes have risks: There is a very fine line to tread between saving and refusing every useful expense.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Sam's reason for changing her buying habits: “I'm trying to ______ right now.”
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Sam says she is trying to “limit my spending” because she is saving for a house deposit.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Which sentence uses the episode's saving expression naturally?

options.text: Sam is saving up for a deposit to buy a house.
Sam is saving down a deposit to rent every product.
Sam is spending up for a deposit without saving.
Sam is depositing up for a save to buy food.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript uses “saving up for a deposit” for gradually collecting the initial payment needed to buy a house.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the description of thrift: living a simple life ______ constantly buying the latest products.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The programme introduces thrift as living simply, “free from the need to” keep buying the latest products.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What does “save up for a rainy day” mean in the programme?
objectiveQuestions.targetExpression: save up for a rainy day

options.text: Keep money for an unforeseen emergency.
Spend all available money before the weather changes.
Buy only products designed for wet weather.
Borrow money whenever a product is on sale.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript explains the phrase as keeping money back in case of unforeseen emergencies.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the programme's collocation: Once people had enough to ______, they could buy non-essential products.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The speaker says people moved towards consumerism once they had enough to meet their basic needs.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Why does Alison say there is “a very fine line to tread” when discussing thrift and consumerism?
objectiveQuestions.targetExpression: a very fine line to tread

options.text: The relationship is complex, so a simple moral judgement may be misleading.
Only one historical definition of thrift has ever existed.
Consumer capitalism has completely removed thrift everywhere.
People must choose between food and shelter as basic needs.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Alison rejects a simplistic view: consumer capitalism has risen, but thrift has not simply disappeared, so the balance is delicate.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the project-budget sentence with today's expression: Keep a small contingency fund and ______.
objectiveQuestions.targetExpression: save up for a rainy day
answers: save up for a rainy day
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The expression transfers naturally from personal finance to keeping resources for an unforeseen project problem.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Which summary best describes how the meaning of thrift changed in the episode?

options.text: It moved from flourishing to frugality and later became linked to social responsibility and changing consumer habits.
It has always meant buying as many luxury products as possible.
It began as a banking term and never had a social meaning.
It changed only because people could no longer meet basic needs.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The programme traces thrift from living well and flourishing to frugality, then to religious, civic, wartime and modern consumer contexts.

assessment.retellingPrompt: Without looking at the full transcript, retell the episode in 80–120 words using this structure: (1) topic—what thrift meant originally; (2) two changes—how religion, society or war connected thrift with frugality and responsibility; (3) modern contrast—what happened after people could afford more than essentials. Phrase bank: “free from the need to”, “meet basic needs”, “a very fine line to tread”. Use at least two phrases naturally. Simple, accurate sentences are enough.
referencePoints: Sam is limiting her spending because she is saving up for a deposit to buy a house.
Thrift can mean living simply, free from the need to keep buying the latest products, and saving for unforeseen emergencies.
The oldest meaning of thrift was connected to thriving or flourishing rather than only saving money.
Puritan and Victorian ideas linked thrift with religious virtue, helping others and being a responsible citizen.
During the Second World War, people were encouraged to avoid waste so resources could support the war effort.
After basic needs were met and living standards rose, consumerism grew, but Alison warns against the simplistic claim that thrift disappeared.
